exam.title: Python — Validated 20Q Data Analysis Final Share
exam.description: Validated 20-question Python share for the 100-question Data Analysis Final blueprint.

questions.question: A variable is assigned `x = 3.14`. Which type is inferred?

options.text: int
float
bool
dict

explanation.ar: 3.14 قيمة عشرية؛ نوعها float.

questions.question: What type of result should a simple condition such as `x > 0` produce?

options.text: List
Boolean
Dictionary
Tuple

explanation.ar: Control flow تختار blocks للتنفيذ بناءً على conditions.

questions.question: A learner expects `range(5)` to include 5. What rule fixes this?

options.text: The start value is excluded
range only works on strings
range always starts at 1
The stop value in range is excluded.

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. for loop تتكرر على sequence مثل list/string/range وتنفذ block لكل item.

questions.question: A student expects loop-else to run after break. What is the correction?

options.text: else always runs twice
break only skips one print
for cannot have else
break prevents the natural-completion else.

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. Loop else تنفذ عند natural completion بدون break.

questions.question: For `[3,5,2,8,1,9,4]`, what maximum is found?

explanation.ar: max_value تبدأ بأول عنصر وتتحدث فقط عند العثور على قيمة أكبر.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Function Definition` according to the taught session?

options.text: A function is a reusable block of code defined to perform a specific task.
Parameters let a function receive values, and `return` sends a result back to the caller.
A default parameter provides a value used when the caller omits that argument.
A function can return multiple values that the caller can unpack into separate variables.

explanation.ar: A function is a reusable block of code defined to perform a specific task.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `map()` according to the taught session?

options.text: `map()` applies a function to each element of an iterable.
`filter()` keeps iterable items for which the supplied function/condition is True.
A recursive function calls itself on smaller subproblems and needs a stopping/base case.
A higher-order function can take another function as an argument or return a function.

explanation.ar: `map()` applies a function to each element of an iterable.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to perform the taught basic email-format check?

options.text: frequency dictionary
"@" in email and "." after @
key=lambda x: ...
sum(numbers) / len(numbers)

explanation.ar: `"@" in email and "." after @` is the course-aligned choice for this task: perform the taught basic email-format check.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `open() & Modes` according to the taught session?

options.text: `open(path, mode)` opens a file; default mode is read (`r`) if omitted.
`file.close()` closes a file object and releases resources; `f.closed` reports whether it is closed.
`read()` reads file content; `read(n)` can read only a limited number of characters.
A `with` statement automatically handles closing the file and reduces resource-leak risk.

explanation.ar: `open(path, mode)` opens a file; default mode is read (`r`) if omitted.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `NumPy ndarray` according to the taught session?

options.text: NumPy provides efficient N-dimensional arrays for numerical computing and forms the base for many data-science libraries.
`shape` is a tuple describing the size of each array dimension.
`np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.
`np.arange()` creates values over a range with an optional step, stopping before the stop value.

explanation.ar: NumPy provides efficient N-dimensional arrays for numerical computing and forms the base for many data-science libraries.

questions.question: What does `np.zeros((2,3))` create?

options.text: A list with two zeros
A 3×2 identity matrix
A 2×3 array filled with zeros
A random array

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. The trace follows the taught `np.zeros()/np.ones()` behavior: `np.zeros()` and `np.ones()` initialize arrays filled with 0 or 1 using a requested shape.

questions.question: Which detail is explicitly provided by `info()`?

options.text: Only mean salary
Only sorted rows
Data types and non-null counts
Only file size

explanation.ar: The trace follows the taught `info()` behavior: `info()` summarizes DataFrame structure including non-null counts and column data types.

questions.question: Which taught function/pattern is most appropriate when you want to add, update or remove DataFrame columns?

options.text: isnull()/fillna()/dropna()
df["new"]=... / df.drop(..., axis=1)
groupby() / apply()
pd.Series(...)

explanation.ar: `df["new"]=... / df.drop(..., axis=1)` is the course-aligned choice for this task: add, update or remove DataFrame columns.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `CSV Loading` according to the taught session?

options.text: The applied workflow loads CSV data into a DataFrame and begins with head/info/describe inspection.
A Boolean condition on the Department column filters the DataFrame to matching employees.
Grouping by Department then taking mean Salary produces average salary for each department.
A new salary column can be calculated vectorially by multiplying Salary by 1.05.

explanation.ar: The applied workflow loads CSV data into a DataFrame and begins with head/info/describe inspection.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Datetime Conversion & Filtering` according to the taught session?

options.text: `pd.to_datetime()` converts the date column before filtering rows after a date threshold.
`to_csv()` writes a DataFrame to a CSV; `index=False` excludes the row index.
The Hospital case study applies inspection, filtering, aggregation, calculated fields, sorting/date logic and export in one workflow.
The Restaurant case study applies Pandas manipulation to sales/customer analysis as an integrated applied workflow.

explanation.ar: `pd.to_datetime()` converts the date column before filtering rows after a date threshold.

questions.question: Which taught tool or pattern is most appropriate when you want to create a highly customizable foundational static 2D plot?

options.text: os.remove(...)
Matplotlib
dict.pop(...)
input(...) without any related analysis step

explanation.ar: السيناريو يطابق الاستخدام المعروض في المصدر؛ الأداة/النمط المناسب هو `Matplotlib`.

questions.question: Which taught tool or pattern is most appropriate when you want to investigate the year with the highest immigration total?

options.text: os.remove(...)
Aggregate by year, identify the maximum, then explore 2010
dict.pop(...)
input(...) without any related analysis step

explanation.ar: السيناريو يطابق الاستخدام المعروض في المصدر؛ الأداة/النمط المناسب هو `Aggregate by year, identify the maximum, then explore 2010`.

source.reference: Slides 23–25 — Peak year / top continents / top countries

questions.question: What do the `s` and `alpha` arguments affect in the styled scatter example?

options.text: The opposite interpretation of the plotted/processed result.
No result can be produced from the taught operation.
Point size and transparency.
It automatically changes the source dataset in an unrelated way.

explanation.ar: Platform clarification based on the taught concept. حسب المثال/المفهوم في المصدر: Point size and transparency..

questions.question: Which statement best describes `Waffle Charts` according to the taught material?

options.text: A Waffle Chart is a grid visualization used to show parts-to-whole relationships; the source describes a 100-square percentage-style grid.
It is presented as a file-system permission command.
It is a Python container whose main purpose is key-value storage.
It is taught as a replacement for every data-analysis step.

explanation.ar: A Waffle Chart is a grid visualization used to show parts-to-whole relationships; the source describes a 100-square percentage-style grid. ده هو الاستخدام/التعريف المدعوم في الجزء المشار له من المصدر.

questions.question: Why create separate positive and negative word clouds in the demonstrated workflow?

options.text: The opposite interpretation of the plotted/processed result.
No result can be produced from the taught operation.
To compare dominant terms in the two feedback groups.
It automatically changes the source dataset in an unrelated way.

explanation.ar: حسب المثال/المفهوم في المصدر: To compare dominant terms in the two feedback groups..
